liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **They Love Each Other** (3 reviews): Reviewer says this song shines, and it is reason enough to download; Bruce takes a precise, beautiful solo and trades phrases with Jerry [19][29][30]
- **Eyes Of The World** (3 reviews): Named as a highlight of the show, along with Wharf Rat; The Hornsby jam after it gets the show moving [20][22][24]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Hornsby's tuning is audible before the song starts [30]
- **New Minglewood Blues** (1 review): Hot version with Bruce tearing it up, seemingly reluctant to stop [30]
- **Tom Thumb's Blues** (1 review): Reviewer dislikes Bruce's accordion playing on this tune [21]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): Jerry and Bruce play hints of Shenandoah and a Bach chorale melody just before it [21]
- **Saint Of Circumstance** (1 review): Very sharp transition from Uncle John's Band opens the second set [24]
- **Space** (1 review): Hornsby drops the So What theme into Space [22]

## Setlist highlights

- **Set I crowd**: rare: 5 archived performances [31]
- **Set II crowd**: back after 879 archived shows (4146 days); rare: 5 archived performances [31]
- **Hornsby - Drums Jam**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [31]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-09-21.172647.me88.rogosa.flac1644** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 146 min [1]
- **gd1991-09-21.150164.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 17 songs; 150 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [3]
- **gd1991-09-21.149996.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: soundboard; 17 songs; 150 min [4]
- **gd91-09-21.sbd.mccall.529.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 145 min; rated 3.71/5 by 14 [12]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this one of the better off-the-board mixes of the era, with Bruce clearly audible; Clean, but reviewer hears signs of a cassette in the lineage despite the stated lineage; Very clean, full, fat soundboard with ambient crowd noise; reviewer calls it borderline excellent [19][20][23][25]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says Hornsby himself admits he is a hack on the accordion [22]
- Hornsby plays keys on nearly every song, with Hell In A Bucket among the exceptions [23]
- Reviewer's first show; arrived by train and only entered the arena around Tom Thumb's [26]
- Less energetic than the previous night's show, though still decent [20]
- The 9.22 show has better sound than this one [23]
- Like other 1991 shows, too much Bruce accordion; by 92/93 the sound was more streamlined [25]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-09-21.172647.me88.rogosa.flac1644**: taped by Dan Rogosa; transferred by Charlie Miller, Mark Goldey; source: 2x Sennheiser ME 88s (stand, OTS) > TCD-D3 > line out > TCD-D5 (Dolby B) [1]. Also: Dan recorded this on DAT and cassette; first of six Boston Garden recordings he made; The circulating DAT version was used to pitch-check this recording and patch Space [1]
- **gd1991-09-21.150164.sbd.cm.miller.flac16**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 26, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [3]. Also: Several sets of masters were combined to make the show complete; this set is 16-bit, 44.1 [3]
- **gd1991-09-21.149996.sbd.pearson-healy.miller.flac2496**: taped by Don Pearson and Dan Healy; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering By Charlie Miller  May 26, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X100) [4]. Also: Several sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [4]
- **gd91-09-21.sbd.mccall.529.sbeok.shnf**: source: sbd> DAT> CD-R> EAC> SHN (no cass in gen) [12]
